gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 13 build now compiles the first landlock ruleset helper lab beside libfs and devres so this security-helper lane is reviewable without pretending it belongs in the live kernel build yet.
The existing Phase 13 make target keeps the bounded ruleset helper lab runnable through the same repeatable tranche gate as the other shared-helper lanes.

The first honest `ruleset.zig` foothold stays in-memory around `landlock_create_ruleset()`, `landlock_union_access_masks()`, `landlock_init_layer_masks()`, `landlock_unmask_layers()`, and the small `build_check_rule()`, `build_check_layer()`, and `build_check_ruleset()` capacity invariants so Zigux can model layer-stack access accounting and representation boundaries before any rb-tree mutation, object references, or live LSM hooks are attempted.

A dedicated Phase 13 test gate now checks both the helper behavior and the survey manifest so future runs can see the current ruleset helper lab and the still-missing deeper kernel state in one place.

A dedicated reviewability gate now ties the ruleset helper descriptor, manifest, and survey note together so this helper-only packet can drift-check its own lane-local evidence without widening into live tree or hierarchy state.
The slice note records the exact helper-first boundary of the new ruleset lab so the lane does not overstate access-mask bookkeeping as full Landlock policy enforcement.
The survey note compares the 719-line `ruleset.c` anchor against the current helper lab and keeps the remaining gap around live tree state and hierarchy lifetime explicit.

The ruleset helper now includes one bounded in-memory planner around `insert_rule()` access extension versus merged-layer intersection so Zigux can exercise the matching-rule branch logic before adding rb-tree storage, locking, or object ownership.

The ruleset helper now adds a small planner for `insert_rule()` tree-search outcomes around `get_root()`, `walker_node`, and the no-match insertion-count branch, keeping the root choice and descent decisions explicit without mutating rb-trees.

The ruleset helper now includes one tiny in-memory planner for the no-match insertion branch around `rb_link_node()` and `rb_insert_color()` after the tree-search outcome is known, keeping the parent or root link mode explicit without mutating live rb-trees.

The ruleset helper now adds one bounded `landlock_find_rule()` lookup planner around root selection, `root->rb_node` descent, and match-versus-null outcomes so Zigux can review read-only rule lookup decisions without mutating live rb-trees, transferring object ownership, or widening into enforcement state.

The ruleset helper now includes one bounded `create_rule()` materialization planner around copied layer stacks, optional merged-layer append behavior, `RB_CLEAR_NODE()` initialization, and whether the key kind would imply object-backed ownership, while still avoiding allocation, live refcounts, or `rb_replace_node()` state.

The ruleset helper now includes one bounded helper-only replacement planning step around `rb_replace_node()`, previous-rule release intent, and inode-only previous-object release intent so matched-rule updates can stay reviewable as data without claiming actual rb-tree mutation or live ownership transfer.

The ruleset helper now includes one bounded `free_rule()` release planner around the unconditional `might_sleep()` boundary, the null-rule early return, `landlock_put_object()` only for inode-backed keys, and `kfree()` intent only when a rule is present, while still avoiding live refcount mutation or deferred workqueue ownership.

The ruleset helper now includes one bounded `merge_tree()` replay planner that validates source single-layer rules, translates them to `dst->num_layers`, and records the pure `insert_rule()` handoff so this packet can review merge handoff data without claiming locked tree traversal, destination access-mask upgrades, or hierarchy ownership.

The next remaining ruleset gap now starts after helper-only replacement, release, and merge-tree replay planning and crosses into actual rb-tree mutation, live object ownership transfer, hierarchy lifetime, workqueue-backed teardown, and other ruleset state that would overstate this helper lab if it were modeled as a pure in-memory followup.
